chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Abul-Husayn Tahir ibn Isma'il al-Khas'ami narrated to us, saying: Abu Kurayb (meaning Muhammad ibn Ala' al-Hamdani) narrated to us, saying: My uncle (meaning Ibn Ubayd al-Tanafisi) narrated to me from Samak ibn Harb, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say:
There will be after me twelve leaders. Then he spoke but what he said was hidden from me, so I asked my father what he said? He said: He said: They are all from Quraysh.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number and lineage of his successors?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *al-Khisal*, establishes the number and tribal origin of the twelve successors (Imams) following the Prophet, a core tenet of Shia eschatology and leadership theology. The specific detail of the Prophet's voice lowering or words becoming indistinct, requiring clarification from his father, highlights the oral transmission's precision in preserving this critical prophecy. Itqan (certainty) regarding the Imams' Qurayshi lineage. This narration serves as a primary textual proof for the twelve Imams, linking the political and spiritual authority directly to the Prophet's family within the Quraysh tribe.
